title: ESXi Host Certificate Expiration
exclusions: Reports the newest complete, successful observation of each governed ESXi host machine SSL certificate when its X.509 `not_after_epoch` is at or before the locally chosen 90-day planning threshold. It does not discover a host absent from authoritative inventory, monitor vCenter MACHINE_SSL_CERT, VMCA roots, solution-user, STS signing, trusted-root, custom service, guest, or third-party certificates, validate trust chains, revocation, key strength, hostname/SAN matching, renewal eligibility, VMCA mode, or prove an outage. Ninety days is a planning policy, not a Broadcom default; Broadcom separately documents vCenter warning/critical settings and a 30-day VCF lifecycle pre-check. Stale, partial, failed, unauthorized, or schema-invalid polls are collection-health findings and cannot prove certificate health. The search performs no renewal, certificate replacement, host reconnect, maintenance action, or compliance attestation.
evidence: After deployment, retain governed vCenter/ESXi inventory; certificate-management mode and owner; approved certificate policy; VCF lifecycle constraints; the version-controlled PowerCLI collector and hash; VCF PowerCLI, vCenter, ESXi, Splunk, and local add-on versions; least-privilege role definition; effective scripted-input and JSON source-type configuration; representative raw observations; independent expected-host, collector-error, schema, duplicate, and freshness reports; the `vmware_esxi_machine_certificate_expiration` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, result rows, alert delivery, and disposition; and dated boundary, expired, future, malformed, stale, duplicate, and missing-host tests. Preserve vCenter, host, certificate scope, subject, issuer, thumbprint, not-before/not-after epochs, collector epoch, snapshot ID, derived days, threshold, event/index time, and source health. These artifacts show what the documented collector and search observed; this documentation-only review created no poll, certificate, Splunk event, alert, renewal, or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a fixed test time, ingest complete `vmware:host_certificate` JSON observations for two governed hosts. Give one a unique machine-SSL thumbprint and `not_after_epoch` exactly 90 days from search time and the other an expiration one second in the past. Expect one warning and one critical row, with `days_remaining` 90 and -1 respectively, after the newest snapshot is selected. Assert host, vCenter, thumbprint, epochs, threshold, collector age, snapshot identity, severity, and UC ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows for a valid certificate more than 90 days away; non-machine-SSL scope; failed or partial collector status; blank host, thumbprint, snapshot, or nonnumeric epochs; not-after not later than not-before; observations older than 36 hours; events outside the window; and an older near-expiry observation superseded by a newer healthy observation. Duplicate delivery of the same snapshot must yield one row. Separate health controls must expose a missing expected host, failed poll, stale snapshot, duplicate identity, and schema drift rather than calling the certificate healthy.

dataSources: A reviewed VCF PowerCLI scripted collector queries vCenter with `Get-VIMachineCertificate -EsxOnly` (or `-VMHost`) and emits one JSON event per ESXi machine SSL certificate per daily complete snapshot to deployment-local `index=vmware`, `sourcetype=vmware:host_certificate`. Required normalized fields are `vcenter`, `host`, `certificate_scope=machine_ssl`, `subject`, `issuer`, lowercase colon-free `thumbprint_sha256`, integer UTC `not_before_epoch`, `not_after_epoch`, `collector_epoch`, unique `snapshot_id`, and `collector_status=ok`. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics and Splunk Add-on for VMware ESXi Logs do not document this certificate contract. Authoritative supporting state is vSphere Client Host > Configure > System > Certificate, VMCA/custom-CA ownership, vCenter certificate mode, VCF pre-check output, and change records.
app: A locally maintained `TA_vmware_certificate_inventory` containing the reviewed VCF PowerCLI scripted input and JSON source-type configuration. A supported Splunk Enterprise or Universal Forwarder may execute and forward it, but Universal Forwarder is a Splunk product rather than Splunkbase app 617. Splunk Add-on for VMware Metrics (Splunkbase 5089) and Splunk Add-on for VMware ESXi Logs (5603) do not supply this poll or normalized source type.
spl:
index=vmware sourcetype="vmware:host_certificate" certificate_scope="machine_ssl" collector_status="ok" earliest=-36h
| eval vcenter=lower(trim(vcenter)), esxi_host=lower(trim(host)), thumbprint_sha256=lower(replace(trim(thumbprint_sha256),":","")), not_before_epoch=tonumber(not_before_epoch), not_after_epoch=tonumber(not_after_epoch), collector_epoch=tonumber(collector_epoch), snapshot_id=trim(snapshot_id)
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(esxi_host)>0 AND len(thumbprint_sha256)=64 AND match(thumbprint_sha256,"^[0-9a-f]{64}$") AND len(snapshot_id)>0 AND isnotnull(not_before_epoch) AND isnotnull(not_after_epoch) AND not_after_epoch>not_before_epoch AND isnotnull(collector_epoch)
| sort 0 vcenter esxi_host -collector_epoch -_indextime
| dedup vcenter esxi_host
| eval collector_age_seconds=now()-collector_epoch
| where collector_age_seconds>=0 AND collector_age_seconds<=129600
| eval days_remaining=floor((not_after_epoch-now())/86400), local_severity=case(not_after_epoch<=now(),"critical",days_remaining<=30,"high",days_remaining<=90,"warning"), planning_threshold_days=90, use_case="UC-2.1.32", expires_utc=strftime(not_after_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), collected_utc=strftime(collector_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| where days_remaining<=planning_threshold_days
| table vcenter esxi_host subject issuer thumbprint_sha256 expires_utc days_remaining local_severity planning_threshold_days collected_utc collector_age_seconds snapshot_id use_case
| sort 0 days_remaining vcenter esxi_host
description: Identifies the X.509 machine SSL certificate presented by each governed ESXi host through a documented PowerCLI snapshot contract. It selects the newest complete observation, calculates whole days to expiry from UTC epochs, and returns certificates inside a local 90-day planning horizon while preserving certificate and snapshot identity.
value: An expired or imminently expiring ESXi machine certificate can interrupt management connectivity and block lifecycle work. A source-honest, host-specific inventory gives platform teams time to coordinate VMCA or custom-CA renewal, confirm root validity and change windows, and avoid confusing certificate collection gaps with healthy status.
implementation: Deploy and qualify the documented daily certificate collector, save the fixed search, and independently monitor expected-host coverage and collector health. Treat 90/30/expired severity bands as local routing policy, compare each result with the host Certificate page and certificate-management authority, and renew only through an approved VMCA or custom-CA procedure after checking root and lifecycle constraints.
visualization: Use a restricted table of vCenter, ESXi host, subject, issuer, SHA-256 thumbprint, expiry UTC, days remaining, severity, snapshot, freshness, owner, certificate mode, and change disposition. Add counts by 0-or-less, 1-30, 31-90, and over-90-day buckets plus a separate expected-host/collector-health panel. Do not label missing rows compliant or mix vCenter/STS/root certificates into this host-only KPI.
schema: Purpose-built JSON ESXi machine-certificate snapshot contract; no applicable CIM dataset
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. No documented CIM dataset preserves ESXi certificate scope, X.509 bounds, SHA-256 thumbprint, collector completeness, and snapshot identity. Keep the raw purpose-built event and independent coverage control.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row is a real threshold result under the qualified snapshot contract. Common nonincident explanations still require evidence:

1. **Approved renewal already scheduled** — preserve the exact host, certificate authority, ticket, owner, window, root validity, and rollback; suppress only notification through that finite window.

2. **Replacement not yet observed** — vCenter/host cache, collector timing, or an incomplete rollout can leave the old thumbprint in Splunk. Compare a fresh PowerCLI result and vSphere Client Certificate page before closing.

3. **Intentional custom-CA lifetime** — corporate certificates can use shorter validity by policy. That changes routing, not the arithmetic; document an owner-approved threshold instead of broadly excluding the CA.

4. **Host inventory transition** — decommissioning, disconnected, or newly attached hosts can create apparent coverage or ownership anomalies. Reconcile authoritative inventory and keep source-health findings visible.

5. **Clock or unit defect** — local-time strings, milliseconds mislabeled as seconds, or collector clock skew can produce extreme days. The contract requires UTC integer seconds and boundary fixtures.

6. **Duplicate routes** — repeated snapshots from two forwarders can repeat a result. The search selects the newest host snapshot; collection health must still remove duplicate routes.

Any suppression must use exact vCenter, host, thumbprint, approved reason, owner, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress expected-host freshness or failed-collector reporting.
detectionType: Newest complete ESXi machine-certificate snapshot inside local expiry horizon
reviewer: Source-backed documentation-only editorial review; production VMware, PKI, and Splunk validation pending

cost.search_load_notes: Daily one-event-per-host certificate inventory and a bounded 36-hour latest-state search.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and certificate boundary

Assign VMware platform, PKI, VCF lifecycle, Splunk, and change owners. Inventory every governed vCenter and ESXi host, certificate authority/mode, root expiry, workload-domain membership, maintenance constraints, owner, and decommission state. Run a supported VCF PowerCLI from a hardened collection tier with HTTPS access to vCenter. Grant only the vCenter privileges proven necessary to read host machine certificate information; the Splunk search account needs read and scheduled-search rights only. Store credentials in the platform credential facility, never script or event output.

Broadcom documents `Get-VIMachineCertificate` as retrieving vCenter and ESXi machine SSL certificate information; use `-EsxOnly` or explicit `-VMHost` so this UC cannot silently mix scopes. Inspect the returned object on every supported PowerCLI/vCenter combination and map actual X.509 properties. Convert UTC dates to Unix seconds once. Do not claim the Metrics or ESXi Logs add-on supplies these fields.

## Step 1 — Build and prove collection

Package a reviewed PowerShell collector in `TA_vmware_certificate_inventory`. For each connected, governed ESXi host emit one compact JSON object with the fields in `dataSources`, one shared `snapshot_id`, and `collector_status=ok` only after the entire intended host enumeration succeeds. Emit errors to a separate source type; never output a partial snapshot as healthy. Configure a daily scripted input in the app's `local/inputs.conf` with the deployment's real index and `sourcetype=vmware:host_certificate`. Use JSON event breaking and UTC timestamps, retain the script hash, and cap permissions.

Compare two hosts with vSphere Client > Hosts and Clusters > host > Configure > System > Certificate and a fresh `Get-VIMachineCertificate -VMHost`. Prove subject, issuer, SHA-256 thumbprint, valid-from, valid-to, host identity, and vCenter. Build independent expected-host and freshness checks from authoritative inventory; disconnected or missing hosts must alert as coverage failures.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save sidecar `spl` verbatim as `vmware_esxi_machine_certificate_expiration` and run after the daily poll. The search accepts only successful machine-SSL observations from 36 hours, normalizes identities, validates a 64-hex SHA-256 thumbprint and numeric epochs, sorts newest first, and selects one host snapshot. It rejects future collectors and snapshots older than 36 hours. `floor((not_after_epoch-now())/86400)` intentionally produces -1 immediately after expiry and whole remaining days before expiry. Exactly 90 days is included; exactly 30 is high; expired is critical. Those bands are local policy, not vendor severity.

Do not broaden the search to vCenter, roots, STS, or trusted certificates without separate identities, ownership, tests, and pages. Keep source-health results separate so a missing certificate never disappears as a healthy zero-row result.

## Step 3 — Validate safely

Use fixed JSON fixtures, not production certificate manipulation. Test valid dates at 91 days, exactly 90 days, 30 days, zero seconds, and one second past; malformed hashes; milliseconds; not-after before not-before; blank identity; duplicate delivery; older/newer conflicting observations; failed/partial status; stale/future collection; and rerun determinism. Assert no floating-day ambiguity at boundaries.

In a nonproduction vCenter, compare result rows to PowerCLI and the host Certificate page. If the owner approves a renewal exercise, capture old/new thumbprints and expiries, VMCA/custom mode, task result, reconnect behavior, and the next complete snapshot. Do not expire or replace a production certificate for testing. Keep draft status until VMware, PKI, VCF, and Splunk owners approve coverage, fixtures, routing, and response.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and respond

Route 31-90 days to planned work, 1-30 days to accelerated change, and expired to the applicable incident path only after confirming raw observation and live state. Before renewal, identify VMCA versus custom mode, root lifetime, lifecycle jobs, host connectivity, compatibility, maintenance requirements, backup/rollback, and certificate subject/SAN policy. Broadcom notes VMCA renewal depends on certificate-management mode and cannot extend past the issuing root; VCF lifecycle checks can require more than 30 days.

Never auto-renew or replace from this search. Close only when authoritative live state and a subsequent complete snapshot show the approved new thumbprint/expiry, related lifecycle checks pass, collection is healthy, and the change record captures impact and rollback.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **No events:** verify authoritative host inventory, vCenter reachability/TLS, credentials, PowerCLI module, scripted-input status, index/RBAC, and collector-error source.
- **Null dates or thumbprint:** inspect the actual cmdlet object and serializer for the deployed versions; do not invent property aliases.
- **Values thousands of years away:** prove Unix seconds rather than milliseconds and UTC rather than locale text.
- **Host differs from UI:** reconcile FQDN, managed-object identity, connected vCenter, stale snapshot, certificate refresh, and duplicate host names.
- **Renew button unavailable:** check vCenter certificate-management mode and custom-CA process; do not bypass governance.
- **Renewed certificate still alerts:** compare thumbprint and poll time, then inspect collector caching, failed partial snapshot, routing delay, and search window.

Retention and thresholds follow local risk policy; this page asserts no universal retention period or unattended remediation.
grandmaExplanation: We check when each virtualization host's secure identity card will expire. The team gets time to renew the right certificate, while missing checks are treated as missing information rather than good news.
hardware: Governed ESXi hosts managed by vCenter. VMCA-managed and custom-CA-managed hosts have different renewal procedures and must be identified before action.
